sigma_analysis_results.rule_description: Detects a Windows program executable started from a suspicious folder
sigma_analysis_results.rule_author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Patrick Bareiss, Anton Kutepov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali

match_context.values: @{CommandLine=%%SystemRoot%%\system32\csrss.exe ObjectDirectory=\Windows SharedSection=1024,20480,768 Windows=On SubSystemType=Windows ServerDll=basesrv,1 ServerDll=winsrv:UserServerDllInitialization,3 ServerDll=sxssrv,4 ProfileControl=Off MaxRequestThreads=16; Image=%%SystemRoot%%\system32\csrss.exe; EventID=1}

sigma_analysis_results.rule_description: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.

attributes.magic: PE32+ executable (console) x86-64, for MS Windows

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The analyzed binary is a legitimate Windows utility, likely tsdiscon.exe (Terminal Services Disconnect), used for managing Remote Desktop Services sessions. Its primary functionality is to disconnect RDP sessions via the Winstation API (WinStationDisconnect). It includes standard administrative features such as command-line parsing for server targets (/server), session enumeration (WinStationGetAllSessionsW), and localization support via utildll.dll. No malicious behaviors such as persistence, unauthorized data exfiltration, or code injection were observed.
